source_packet.selected_slice: Does a material change in a UCITS fund investment objective, policy or restriction require prior SFC approval under this circular, taking account of product features, home requirements and the application transition?

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

authority_field_contract.meaning: This field concerns ADDITIONAL EXTERNAL DEPENDENCIES, not the source passage already quoted in source_support.
authority_field_contract.AVAILABLE: Use only for at least one supplied external dependency ID with a non-null source_hash; never put a source unit_id here.
authority_field_contract.NONE_DECLARED: Use [] when this claim needs no additional external dependency; cite the circular in source_support instead.
authority_field_contract.MISSING: Identify missing external dependencies, not the cited circular passage. If a needed authority has no identifiable supplied dependency ID, retain [] and name the missing authority in followup_questions. Never invent a catalogue match.
authority_field_contract.UNCERTAIN: Retain uncertainty about which additional external authority is necessary.

question.question: Does the selected material post-authorisation investment change satisfy the substantive, commencement and pending-application conditions for removal of SFC prior approval under the proposed transition reading?
question.unit_of_assessment: One material change to an investment objective, policy or restriction in a post-authorisation matter for a UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, or a UK-domiciled scheme authorised as UK UCITS, including its application history.
question.actor: The covered UCITS fund seeking relief from the SFC’s prior-approval requirement.
question.temporal_basis: The assessment date must be on or after 28 November 2025. An application received before that date with neither approval nor authorisation granted by that date is treated as an exclusion from relief.
question.true_means: Within scope, home requirements are met, none of novelty, complexity or possible local policy implications applies, commencement has occurred, and no pending pre-effective application excludes relief. Continuing notification and post-vetting duties are not assessed.
question.false_means: Within scope, the proposed removal is unavailable; this does not independently establish an approval obligation or non-compliance. Outside scope no determination is supplied; unknown inputs remain unknown.

candidates.representation:
Declared output convention: TRUE_IS_SATISFIED
Used facts:
defined_ucits_fund: The fund is a UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, or a UK-domiciled collective investment scheme authorised as UK UCITS. (truth value)
post_authorisation_change: The selected change is a post-authorisation matter for the fund. (truth value)
material_investment_change: The selected change is material and concerns the fund's investment objective, policy or restriction. (truth value)
assessment_date: Date as of which availability of the selected removal of prior approval is assessed. (Gregorian calendar date)
home_requirements_met: The selected change complies with the fund's applicable home-jurisdiction requirements. (truth value)
novel_features: The selected change involves novel product features. (truth value)
complex_features: The selected change involves complex product features. (truth value)
possible_local_policy_implications: The selected change may have local policy implications; this asks about possibility, not only established actual effects. (truth value)
pending_pre_effective_application: An application concerning the selected change was received by the SFC before 28 November 2025 and had received neither approval nor authorisation by that date. (truth value)
Scope: all of these conditions hold: [the fact defined_ucits_fund; the fact post_authorisation_change; the fact material_investment_change]
Result: all of these conditions hold: [[the fact assessment_date] is greater than or equal to [date value 2025-11-28]; the fact home_requirements_met; it is not the case that [at least one of these conditions holds: [the fact novel_features; the fact complex_features; the fact possible_local_policy_implications]]; it is not the case that [the fact pending_pre_effective_application]]
Result type: bool
Supplied classifications requiring judgment: defined_ucits_fund, post_authorisation_change, material_investment_change, home_requirements_met, novel_features, complex_features, possible_local_policy_implications, pending_pre_effective_application. Their assessment is not implemented by this formula.
Runtime semantics: Missing or temporally unavailable facts evaluate as UNKNOWN. For Boolean conjunction FALSE dominates UNKNOWN; for disjunction TRUE dominates UNKNOWN; otherwise uncertainty is retained, and NOT UNKNOWN is UNKNOWN. A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch. A false scope returns OUT_OF_SCOPE; an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN; an unknown IF condition returns UNKNOWN without choosing either branch. No UNKNOWN, CONFLICT or ERROR is converted to a known Boolean.
